comparator.name: History (Geschiedenis)
comparator.academicYear: 2026–27 public curriculum for a Fall 2026 entrant
comparator.sourceNotes: The current UvA programme table lists 60 EC in each year: 60 EC of first-year historical periods, historiography and a 12-EC introductory research seminar; 48 EC of named second-year courses and 12 EC open choice; 30 EC of named third-year advanced work and thesis plus 30 EC open choice. The 42 EC of combined second/third-year open choice may be used for courses, a minor, internship or approved exchange. This comparison preserves those unchosen spaces rather than assigning invented subjects. The 12-EC independent history thesis is distinct from the earlier seminar and advanced research modules. UvA offers both full-time and part-time registration; the 180-EC full-time pathway is represented.
components: Independent historical inquiry based on secondary literature.
Digital collection, structuring and analysis of historical sources.
Verdiepingsvak II: concepten in de geschiedenis
Genuinely free elective space, including an optional minor or exchange.

core: Global and European historical periods, political and social change
Historical research, source criticism, historiography and independent thesis
Historical connections to contemporary societies, politics and international relations
adjacent: Material culture, archaeology, art and heritage as historical evidence
Public history, memory and communicating the past across media
questions: How do different sources and public narratives change our understanding of the past?

alternatives.label: Historical change, sources and cultures
alternatives.concept: A broad historical inquiry spanning modern societies, empires, gender, war, Indigenous history, archaeology and material culture, with source interpretation and an advanced history research seminar. Art history, politics and narrative provide specific complementary historical lenses rather than substitute for UvA’s specialist history sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed schedule combines all six UCR History courses with archaeology, art history, historically situated literature, politics and source interpretation.
progression: History and art-history introductions precede advanced seminar, museums and heritage where feasible; all six term offerings, formal prerequisites, 24 unique courses, four per term and eight 300-level courses were checked against the current enriched workbook.

alternatives.label: History, heritage and public memory
alternatives.concept: Uses historical research and material heritage to examine how museums, film, television, podcasts and public rhetoric interpret the past for communities. This shifts advanced study toward public history and communication while retaining UCR’s six History courses.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed schedule retains the history and heritage core and adds documentary, media, race and community rhetoric as substantive public-history practice.
alternatives.distinctness: Six courses differ in each direction: the public-memory route adds Introduction to Film & Media, From T.V. to TikTok, Media & Race, Qualitative Research Methodology and two rhetoric courses, while removing Greek Archaeology, two politics courses and three literary interpretation courses. The shift changes both evidence and audience, not merely the label.
progression: Introductions to film, media, history and art precede documentary, museums and history research; all six term offerings, formal prerequisites, 24 unique courses, four per term and seven 300-level courses were checked against the current enriched workbook.

candidates.label: Heritage and public history across museums and media

selection.assessment: The closest programme covers all direct-interest rows in broad historical inquiry. Public history is an explicit UvA direction and supports a genuinely different UCR route through heritage, media and community presentation. A third route focused on antiquity and the Middle Ages lacks enough UCR specialist period-history and primary-language training for a coherent 24-course historical specialization; padding it with general adjacent courses would be misleading. Stop at two.

notes.text: UvA allocates 138 EC to named historical study and 42 EC to open choices, including a 12-EC bachelor thesis and sustained source-based research. UCR offers six History courses and relevant archaeology, art history, media and political inquiry; neither UCR path reproduces the full chronology, digital historical laboratory, intensive historical theory or required independent thesis. The optional UCR research opportunity is shown separately from scheduled courses.
